races.name: Dickie McGuinness Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: Won twice over 2m on Good and Soft with Brian Hayes aboard for the powerful Mullins stable — best form is over further, raising a stamina question at 2m1f, but the Good ground is fully suitable and a hold-up style means it needs a faster-run race than this shape is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Karlynn
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 2m4f most recently and placed at 2m2f, giving genuine claims that the trip is within range; races prominently, which suits the expected controlled tempo, and John Burke's stable is 0/2 in the 14-day window but the horse's own form profile is competitive.

runners_data.name: Evangelic
runners_data.note: Trainer Watson is 0/2 in the 14-day period and recent hurdles form reads 7-0-0 with no placing in the past three; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, the crowded back-end of this field means securing even a midfield berth will be a task, and the horse has not shown the acceleration to compensate in this company.

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained with multiple good-ground placings and a front-runner's habit of racing close to the pace, blinkers fitted — the 90-day absence is a minor query but the profile fits this shape well if the second run for the yard brings the expected sharpening.

runners_data.name: Pebble Island
runners_data.note: 203 days off the track (a 14-furlong flat run was the most recent, flagged), form shows a placed effort on Good ground over shorter but the limited hurdles experience (6-U) introduces uncertainty; in truth a hold-up horse by inclination who has been placed in midfield on the map, and the long absence tempers confidence in it finding a natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 12f and has placed form, but the 190-day absence (a 42-furlong jumps run) is a significant fitness concern; by nature a hold-up horse reassigned to midfield due to the crowded rear, its best hope is a pace collapse rather than a tactical move.

runners_data.name: Yup Bro
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher at the wrong end of fields — 12th, 13th, 12th, 11th in recent runs — and flagged for fading finishes; headgear (hood) worn and a hold-up style that has not converted into any placing on its recent record make this a non-factor unless the race falls apart entirely.

runners_data.name: Tex Amare
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and likely to get a straightforward lead; only one run on record (3rd on Soft over 2m) so the step to 2m1f on Good is an open question, but the lightest weight in the field at 147lbs and an uncontested lead are concrete positional advantages for Dylan O'Connor.

races.paceDynamic: Tex Amare is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, should control proceedings from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Bellewstown. The prominent types Karlynn and Mino Des Mottes will likely slot in close behind, creating an orderly pace that neither truly tests the front-runner nor generates the late surge that hold-up horses require. With the pace steady rather than searching, horses racing prominently and able to quicken off a controlled tempo are best positioned, while true hold-up horses will struggle to find the gaps or the momentum to peel off the back of a slowly-run race. This race shape strongly favours the prominent and lead profile — those who can travel close to Tex Amare and produce a clean jump at the last will have a decisive positional advantage. The field also holds more hold-up types than the map accommodates: Puppet Master, Pebble Island, and Evangelic are genuine closers forced into midfield roles, making it unlikely all three secure their natural position, with Puppet Master's trainer angle and Pebble Island's hurdling form making them the likelier of the trio to adapt.

watchPoints.text: Tex Amare goes uncontested to the front — if Dylan O'Connor is allowed to control and conserve from flagfall, the lead horse is a serious danger at every stage of this race.
Beauvallon's hold-up style and Brian Hayes' experience could be decisive in the straight if the pace quickens — watch for Hayes switching wide between the last two hurdles to manufacture a clear run.

Puppet Master and Pebble Island both carry significant lay-offs (190 and 203 days respectively) and are hold-up horses squeezed into midfield; either could interfere with rivals if they jump erratically early, creating traffic issues for the prominent runners.
Karlynn is the only runner to have won on Good ground at this trip range recently and races prominently — if Tex Amare ties up before the last, Karlynn is the most naturally positioned beneficiary.

Yup Bro's record of fading badly in finish suggests it may drift wide or lose its position turning for home — jockeys on hold-up horses should note the potential for a loose cannon in the rear half of the field.

races.name: Grimme Ireland Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Laxxio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Anthony Mullins with a mixed recent record including a fall; two placings on Good ground in 17f+ suggest this trip is fine, but 77 days off and patchy form over bigger fields is a concern.

runners_data.name: Loyal Touch
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type who has run 6th or worse in every hurdle start; four runs on Good going without a place is damning, and a 51-day break (including a fall) does not help Denis Hogan's chances.

runners_data.name: Press The Button
runners_data.note: Prominent rider Keith Donoghue suits this Gavin Cromwell-trained gelding; won on Good ground at this distance and the tongue-tie has been fitted previously — course-fresh over a trip he's placed at twice, one of the most compelling profiles here.

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Prominent type from Andrew Slattery who showed a hint of form with a recent third over this trip on Good; lightweight at 162lbs and consistent without threatening, better suited to a strongly-run race.

runners_data.name: Pepper Noir
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning after a 537-day absence — that huge layoff is extremely hard to overcome, especially with a form string of U0 and a jockey claim (Clarke 7lb); very difficult to trust.

runners_data.name: Allroadsleadtorome
runners_data.note: John McConnell's runner by nature wants to come from off the pace, but the surplus of hold-up horses in this field means he'll likely sit in midfield rather than his preferred rearward pitch — that compromise dims his already modest recent form (5-579).

runners_data.name: Highland Realm
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Willie Mullins four-year-old with a single run to his name — a promising second on Good ground over this trip — and 323 days since; the stable form is live and the profile suits sitting prominent on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: Consistent performer who has placed in six of ten hurdle starts on Good ground; runs prominently and T Hogan sends him out without a run in 25 days, making him one of the more reliable each-way profiles in the field given his frequency of placing.

runners_data.name: Million Dollar Man
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner; recent form reads P-60 which is modest, but his role is to dictate rather than win — an uncontested lead on Good ground could allow him to outrun his odds if rivals underestimate him.

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type from S Michael Millar with nine runs on Good going without a win; the "fades in finish" warning compounds the concern that he'll stay on without threatening in a scenario that doesn't set up perfectly for closers.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: By natural inclination a hold-up horse who prefers to come late, his best recent effort was a second over 17f on Good; pushed forward in mapping terms by the field's shape, he's less likely to get his preferred race from this position.

runners_data.name: Matcho d'Agrostis
runners_data.note: Style unknown with a form string of F-F0 including two falls; finishes poorly in the data (flagged as fading) and Paul Nolan sends him with 28 days' rest — too many question marks for a maiden with better-exposed options.

runners_data.name: The Flying Rambler
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown quantity for J P Dempsey with a single outing (seventh on Good); the hold-up tag and "lightly raced" flag mean there is almost no data to work with — impossible to assess confidently.

runners_data.name: Wackestone
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the mount for Gordon Elliott, which is an immediate upgrade in ride quality; placed twice on Good ground and prominent in style, though the 89-day absence and "fades in finish" concern temper confidence.

runners_data.name: Double Order
runners_data.note: True back-marker by inclination mapped to midfield only because of the race's shape; the "fades in finish" flag is an added complication, and form of 9-60 on Good gives Ian Donoghue's runner very little to build a case on.

runners_data.name: Getaway Tobin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from John McConnell who placed fifth and fourth in his last two Good-ground runs over this trip; stable has three runners which could affect tactics, but he's one of the sounder hold-up types if closers are to land a blow.

runners_data.name: G N Jefferson
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up horse from Jack Teal with the fade flag attached; one run at Bellewstown course form goes against him and form of 43-0 suggests he's running out of improvement at this level.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Patrick Rooney with no form, no going data, and an amateur jockey claim; going listed as UNKNOWN and entirely unknown quantity — lowest confidence of any runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as fading in finish with a single hurdles run of 12th on Good; jumping form on the level is better but that doesn't transfer, and D Buckley's yard has had minimal recent winners.

races.paceDynamic: Million Dollar Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19, and with no rival likely to push him hard from the off, he should be able to dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop around Bellewstown's tight turning track. The early pace will be honest but not searching, meaning the race will be truly run from the front with any acceleration coming from the second-last hurdle home. This controlled scenario strongly favours horses who can track the leader in the first three or four, with enough stamina to pick up off a genuine but unspectacular gallop — prominent racers with proven Good-ground form at this trip are best placed. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Double Order, Allroadsleadtorome, and Kasper Hauser all genuine back-markers by nature but forced into a midfield map position given race shape; Press The Button and Highland Realm are far better placed to secure prominent berths and use them.

scenarios.body: If Million Dollar Man's unchallenged lead turns into a winning advantage as rivals misjudge the race and leave it too late.

watchPoints.text: Million Dollar Man sets the entire pace dynamic alone — if he jumps well and gets a soft lead from the front, the race could be far more truly run than odds suggest, inflating the chance of prominent stalkers Press The Button and Highland Realm.

With 19 runners over Bellewstown's tight track, crowding and jumping errors at the early hurdles are a real risk — horses like Matcho d'Agrostis (two previous falls) and The Flying Rambler (unknown jumper) could cause disruption to the chasing pack.
Pepper Noir returns from 537 days off and Willows Word makes her debut — both could jump unpredictably and are positioned to cause interference for other runners in a field this large.

The McConnell yard saddles three runners (Allroadsleadtorome, Getaway Tobin, Highland Realm) — watch for any market moves suggesting which stable runner is most fancied, as the trainer's attention may be concentrated on one lead horse.

Hopeful Hero's consistency (six placings in ten Good-ground hurdle runs) stands out in a maiden field of this size — if the prominent-tracking scenario plays out, his profile suggests he will be placed again even if not winning.

races.name: Street Sweep Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Becasse
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's five-year-old brings course-and-distance placed form on Good and is genuinely mapped rearward here — not by nature but because midfield horses without strong pace commitment have been filtered to the back; the key angle is freshness (33 days) and a jockey in Darragh O'Keeffe who can place a horse late.

runners_data.name: Fiver Friday
runners_data.note: Won twice over this course and distance and recent form on Good ground reads 13/15 — Donoghue is well placed to claim one of the prime tracking positions behind Barbizon; concern is the 77-day absence and a 14-day trainer strike rate of just 1/32.

runners_data.name: Ifiwerearichman
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with proven Good-ground credentials (2W4P in similar conditions) and a placed return 38 days ago; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a genuine asset in an OR-125 handicap and the horse's consistent prominent style should mean he gets his position in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed pace-setter and therefore the most important horse tactically; his STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects that his role here is not his ideal mode — he is essentially doing the race a service — but a 116-day absence and two previous wins on Good are the real variables to weigh.

runners_data.name: Encanto Bruno
runners_data.note: Consistent each-way performer over Good ground (4W7P sim-going, 11/15 qualifying runs) ridden by a 7lb claimer which offsets OR-124; has run well fresh and the recent 19-day turnaround points to being primed rather than rushed.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: Won over this trip on Good and the prominent style should see him track the pace, but a trainer T14 of 0/4 and the wide handicap (8605-3 recent) make it hard to be bullish; Daniel King is relatively unfancied in this company.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: Registered two wins on Good and the form figures 1-1 at these conditions are strong; C Byrnes has a poor T14 (0/13) but Spy's natural jumping style and recent winning form (1 at 33 days) make him one of the more interesting horses behind Barbizon.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: A natural front-of-field racer whose instinct is to be prominent, but the density of this field means Enright will likely find him squeezed back well off his preferred spot; STYLE_FIT 0.92 reflects the displacement cost and 67-day absence adds another query.

runners_data.name: Lisnamult Lad
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old partnered by an amateur at OR-122 and his recent form string (FP9P-P) is extremely concerning; the prominent style is fine in theory but his jumping record raises serious doubts about getting round in a 19-runner handicap hurdle.

runners_data.name: Red Glory
runners_data.note: Three wins from six on Good and a recent win 20 days ago gives De Bromhead a live second string here; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim is worth taking seriously and the horse's hurdle form suggests he copes with a prominent position without exerting himself early.

runners_data.name: Come On The Lads
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural instinct will be frustrated by the size of this field — he wants to race in the first four but is likely to end up sixth to eighth at best; Cromwell's T14 of 6/45 is solid and the 18f win on Soft is encouraging, though STYLE_FIT 0.93 flags the tactical compromise.

runners_data.name: Malbay Madness
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good and hold-up headgear (hg:h) means this is one runner who might actually benefit from being held up; OR-121 and P J O'Hanlon's ride are the limiting factors but the horse's recent form (773-11) is genuinely eye-catching.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: The soft-ground form (four of five qualifying runs on Soft) is an obvious concern on Good today; a prominent type pushed into midfield against her will adds a further layer of difficulty, and 91-day absence makes this feel like a retrieval run rather than a winning bid.

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: One of several prominent horses absorbed into midfield — Cian Quirke will need to be proactive early to find any position of influence; the Good-ground record (3W5P from 8/14) is decent but the 63-day gap and OR-121 make this look like a likely place-at-best candidate.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who arrives fresh (28 days) and the form 455-PU hides a sound fifth over this trip on Good; Cromwell's yard has been busy (T14 8/58) and this is the runner most naturally suited to racing off a genuine pace — if the field tires, Finegan can deliver late.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy on a Gordon Elliott five-year-old at OR-119 commands attention but the horse is a natural prominent type racing out of role here; STYLE_FIT 0.93 flags the map displacement and the recent form (10-632) suggests he finds one or two too good rather than hitting the front.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Two Good-ground wins in five qualifying runs and a winning return 39 days ago; a prominent type pushed back by the weight of numbers, but Mullins has history of placing horses to run well fresh — if Paul's Dream can box clever and find a good line through, STYLE_FIT 0.91 is less of a handicap than it looks.

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Consistent performances on Good ground (14/15 qualifying runs) but placed form rather than winning form (2W4P) tells the story; OR-114 and a 7lb claimer on an eight-year-old who is naturally prominent but displaced here makes this a competitive fringe candidate at best.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: No jockey listed at time of analysis, which is a red flag in itself; the form (554/0-) over longer trips and the absence of any recent strong form on Good (0W1P in sim-going) places this firmly in the lower tier of winning chances regardless of race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Barbizon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, critically, has no rival willing to press him for the lead — he sets out from the front and controls the tempo on Good ground at Bellewstown, a track that suits a judicious gallop-setter. The field behind him is overwhelmingly prominent in profile: Fiver Friday, Ifiwerearichman, Spy, Encanto Bruno, Putapoundinthejar, Red Glory and Lisnamult Lad all want to race close to the pace, meaning the first two furlongs will see a fierce scramble for tracking positions behind Barbizon, stretching the field and creating natural pressure on the pace without any horse deliberately forcing it. This field carries far more pace than the map can accommodate — Autumn Twist, Thisistheway, Missus Beeton, Come On The Lads, Playtime and Paul's Dream are all genuine prominent types who will be shuffled back into mid-to-rear positions against their natural inclination, with Spy, Red Glory and Fiver Friday the most likely to actually secure front-rank spots behind Barbizon given form and jockey authority. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit handily in fifth to eighth and travel sweetly without fighting for position — a prominent-to-midfield profile who finds a rhythm early, avoids the early scrimmage, and picks up off a genuine but controlled gallop will be best placed.

watchPoints.text: Barbizon's front-running role is the single most important tactical factor in this race — if he is allowed a soft lead and sets a sustainable tempo, the horses tracking him (Spy, Red Glory, Fiver Friday) are immediately advantaged, so watch the early market moves on those three.

Lisnamult Lad (Mr T J Stafford, amateur) is a potential jumping hazard in a 19-runner hurdle field — a fall or unseating in the pack behind Barbizon could compromise several prominent horses and alter the race shape entirely.

Malbay Madness showed back-to-back wins on Good recently and the hold-up headgear could see P J O'Hanlon drop away quietly before delivering late — this horse's recent form spike is easily overlooked in a big field and deserves monitoring in-running.

The cluster of STYLE_FIT-flagged prominent types (Autumn Twist, Come On The Lads, Thisistheway, Playtime) will all be competing for the same mid-pack positions in the opening half-mile — watch which of them settles most easily, as the one that accepts its position without fighting the bridle is the live outsider threat.

Stuntman Steve is the only confirmed hold-up horse with a realistic winning profile if the pace scenario unravels — Eoghan Finegan (5lb claim) tracking the field from the rear bears monitoring from the second-last if any gaps open up between the tiring prominent types.

races.name: Johnny's Race Day Mares Maiden Hurdle
holdup: Uno Me I Like My T

runners_data.name: Bold Reflection
runners_data.note: Veteran of 8 years racing in P style with a win at 16f on Heavy and a recent flat effort (P-0), she fades in the finish and this extended 2m4½f Good-ground trip looks to stretch her stamina; McConnell yard is 0/27 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Jack Kennedy aboard — a potent booking — showing consistency at 19f on Good (three runs, twice placed); the hg:h headgear suits a bold jumping front-runner over this stiff 2m4½f trip.

runners_data.name: Chisel Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking type whose best effort was a runner-up at 20f on Good, giving her a direct profile match for this trip and going; Donoghue yard quiet at T14:0/17 but the horse's form arc is improving (6-4-2).

runners_data.name: Everyday Life
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only one run logged (9th at 19f Good), the fade-in-finish flag and unknown style makes this a speculative runner in a large field; Donoghue's second string here.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a third at 22f on Good in her most recent run, giving her the clearest stamina credentials among the H-style runners; the tp headgear suggests she needs restraining, and a truly-run race suits her profile well.

runners_data.name: Glendaars Crystal
runners_data.note: Two runs, both at 16f on Good, both out of the frame (7th, 11th) — the step up to 2m4½f is untested and the lightly-raced flag adds significant uncertainty; McLoughlin yard at T14:0/6.

runners_data.name: Idaho Expresso
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with an uncertain style and a chequered form string (U13P-P), the single run on Good at 19f gives no confidence; Christie yard at T14:0/1 offers little support in this competitive maiden.

runners_data.name: Jet To Glory
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner whose battle with Ardeen Joy for the early lead is the defining tactical question of this race; two runs on Good at 18f and 16f both produced placed efforts (4th, 5th), suggesting stamina for 2m4½f may be marginal.

runners_data.name: Jo's Secret
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a strong recent form profile — two placed efforts at 16f on Good and a second at 16f — the t headgear suits a horse who travels up with the pace, and four of six career runs on similar ground indicates versatility.

runners_data.name: Red Acres Georgie
runners_data.note: A 140-day absence is a serious flag, and two runs on relevant going have both produced 7th-place finishes; hold-up style suits a truly-run race but the lengthy layoff demands caution before making a strong case.

runners_data.name: Riverwoods
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's prominent racer has a strong pace-fit profile — two placed efforts in four Good-ground runs including a third at 16f most recently — and the T14:11/35 rate signals a yard in form; the step to 2m4½f is the main unknown.

runners_data.name: She's All Talk Sir
runners_data.note: No available form, unknown going preference, no LR data supplied — a complete unknown in a field of 19, making assessment impossible beyond style flag (U).

runners_data.name: Star Of Idaho
runners_data.note: Single run on Good (4th at 16f) for the powerful Mullins yard currently operating at T14:10/56; lightly raced and unexposed over this longer trip, the stable form is the main reason to treat this runner with respect.

runners_data.name: Uno Me I Like My T
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fade-in-finish warning and a form string littered with pulled-up and fell symbols (0P-F3F); three of four recorded runs on Good produced poor performances and this 153lb burden over 2m4½f looks demanding.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Elliott's second string alongside Ardeen Joy, sitting prominently behind the leaders at T14:9/43 for the yard; two fifth-place finishes on Good at 19f and 16f suggest a solid but unspectacular performer who needs something to go wrong ahead.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at age 4, single run at 19f on Good (9th) with a fade-in-finish tag; the lightly-raced flag and inexperience over 2m4½f make this a developmental run at best.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but the fade-in-finish flag appears repeatedly and three recorded runs have all produced double-figure positions; Good-ground form at 22f shows willingness to stay but the level of form is modest.

runners_data.name: How's Ellie
runners_data.note: A 221-day absence is the dominant headline here — returning from a very long break for the Mullins yard (T14:9/51) and two previous runs at 16f on Soft and Good both produced fifths; class of trainer makes the comeback angle worth noting.

runners_data.name: Prophetess Miriam
runners_data.note: Prominent type with the most encouraging form among the field's placers — two wins/placings at 16f on Good and a fourth in the same going — and four of five runs on similar ground suggest genuine Good-ground reliability over shorter; the step up to 2m4½f is the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Jet To Glory and Ardeen Joy are both confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner maiden hurdle over 2m4½f on Good ground at Bellewstown, and both will look to establish themselves at the head of affairs from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than any stolen stroll. Western Shores and Chisel Hill will press from prominent positions, adding further pressure to the early sections and ensuring the pace holds through the middle stages of this staying test. With two genuine lead-seekers fighting for the front, the race is unlikely to be run at a false or slowly-run tempo, and the sustained gallop over this distance on Good ground will place a premium on stamina and jumping accuracy rather than raw speed. This shape — honest, front-contested, run at a true pace over an extended trip — firmly favours horses who can travel prominently without burning fuel, or hold-up types with the class and stamina to reel in a genuinely run race in the closing stages; pure front-runners burning hard early are at risk, while prominent-to-midfield types with proven good-ground form over 2m+ are the primary beneficiaries.

Riverwoods (De Bromhead, T14:11/35) is the most prominent-style runner with a proven yard behind it — if the pace is genuinely run, watch for Darragh O'Keeffe to slot just behind the duel and inherit a winning position from the second fence out.
How's Ellie returns after 221 days for Mullins (T14:9/51) — a stable that rarely runs horses cold without expectation; watch the market for any move that signals she is ready to win first time back.

Star Of Idaho is another Mullins runner (T14:10/56) with only one career run and an unknown ceiling — lightly raced types from powerful yards in large-field maiden hurdles are classically hard to assess, and a big run at a price is plausible.

races.paceDynamic: Clone Cross is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should establish a controlled, unhurried gallop on good ground over 2m4½f at Bellewstown — a course that rewards those who travel well in behind before the final climb. Hitthehayson and Codger's Rock are the most likely to press from prominent positions, while Hurricane Hero and Georginas Jet will look to track the front group, but none carries the same front-running intent as Clone Cross. The field holds significantly more prominent and hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear: Mother Ship, Agent Tequila, Ballinagaine Girl, and Lost Features are all genuine hold-up horses who are likely to be nudged into midfield rather than their natural rearward berths, meaning traffic and interference risk increases through the early and middle sections. With a single leader setting a sustainable tempo and a bunched midfield likely to compress approaching the turn for home, the race shape favours well-handicapped prominent racers who can travel close to the pace without expending energy in a cavalry charge, and who carry enough class and fitness to quicken off a sound gallop in the straight.

Mother Ship and Ballinagaine Girl are both trained by John Joseph Hanlon with the same yard in strong form (combined 5/37 T14) — watch for stable tactics as two genuine hold-up types navigating the same congested midfield could interfere with each other.|

My Policy returns from a 436-day absence and, while historically placed on good ground, an unknown fitness level in a 19-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4½f is a significant risk — watch for signs of weakness jumping or in the straight.|

With 19 runners, the hurdles down the back straight are a serious traffic flashpoint — horses tagged with redistribution (Agent Tequila, Lost Features, Mother Ship, Ballinagaine Girl) are racing in a tighter pocket than they prefer and any fallers in the first half of the race could trap several of them.|

Pourquoi Poi is 1W2P from 8 runs on good ground with a 4lb claim from Benjamin Kennedy — watch whether the tongue tie entry (previously worn) and the step up in field size relative to recent runs affects his usual prominent hold and travel.|

races.paceDynamic: Lisnagar Fortune is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, critically, faces no serious challenge for the lead — giving Alex Harvey the chance to dictate an unchallenged, measured gallop over 3m½f on Good ground at Bellewstown. With just one pace-setter controlling proceedings, the tempo is likely to be honest rather than brutal, which typically rewards horses that can track close to the pace and sustain their effort into the finish rather than closers who need a genuine test of stamina. Outside The Door, Burning Ability, Ottoman Style, Jisco Du Brem and Le Kap are genuine front-of-field types who should settle comfortably in the slipstream, while the hold-up brigade of Dorans Law and Whatsavailable must hope the gallop is strong enough to bring them into contention late. The field holds more prominent-running types than can realistically all secure that position — Radar Ahead, The Miracle Man, Midnight Moonshine, Mavetherave, Tolka Row, Accustomed and Broken Ice are all natural prominent horses but several must sit deeper than they would prefer, with Radar Ahead and The Miracle Man the most likely to press hard for a handy berth given jockey class. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent hold-and-race types who can settle just off Lisnagar Fortune and kick from the second-last — the winner is most likely to come from that bracketed group on the heels of a controlled leader.

watchPoints.text: Lisnagar Fortune's early position is the race-shaper — if he is allowed to dictate entirely unchallenged, those tracking him (Outside The Door, Jisco Du Brem) get a soft lead and the hold-up horses may never get close enough.

Radar Ahead and The Miracle Man will both try to push forward from their redistributed midfield slots — watch the first half-mile to see if either breaks out of the pack and injects pace, which would materially change the tempo.

Mephisto's 278-day absence combined with a visor and a step up to the longest trip of his career is a combination of risks — if he stops quickly from 2 out he could cause interference in a tightly-packed field.

Dorans Law and Whatsavailable are the only genuine hold-up types in a field that is otherwise saturated with prominent runners — their fate depends entirely on whether the pace is honest enough over 3m½f on Good ground, so watch the sectionals through the back straight.

Jack Kennedy's booking for The Miracle Man stands out in terms of jockey quality relative to the horse's OR of 105 — if Kennedy pushes forward to claim a prominent position early, The Miracle Man becomes a more significant factor than the redistribution tag alone suggests.
